body.statement: There is an explicit expression for \(K_\Sigma=K_\Sigma(d,m,\gamma,L,d_{\max})\), obtained from the coarse spectral-density resolvent, such that for every \(n\ge3\), \(\Pr\{(M_0,M_1)\in\mathcal C_n^M(\alpha)\}\ge1-\alpha\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cmp}}(d,m,G;\gamma,L,d_{\min},d_{\max})\). One admissible calibration is certified by \(\|H_{\ell ij}\|_{\mathrm F}\le n^{-1/2}\), \(\|H_{\ell ij}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le n^{-1}\), Gaussian quadratic-form tails, and the radius \(r_n=2K_\Sigma\{\sqrt{\log(4d^2/\alpha)/n}+\log(4d^2/\alpha)/n\}\); verified rational outward rounding can only enlarge the region.
body.justification: This closes the finite-sample calibration bottleneck needed for honest inference at singular and unidentified laws.
body.gap: Basu and Michailidis control Gaussian Gram matrices, Hsu et al. control quadratic forms, and Giurcanu and Spokoiny give scalar covariance bands; none supplies this joint multivariate lag region with explicit compact-class constants and exact-computation rounding.
body.consumer: Any branch-free transfer certificate can be inverted with advertised finite-sample coverage, including near root collisions where Wald approximations fail.
